purpose: Field-level primary-source evidence batch for Germany, France and Spain.

records.claim: Germany's student visa/residence route requires admission to a recognised educational institution and the applicant must satisfy the applicable visa and residence conditions for study.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Federal Foreign Office guidance for studying in Germany.

records.claim: For a German student visa, financial support may be demonstrated through parental finances, a declaration of commitment, a German blocked account, a bank guarantee or qualifying scholarship funding.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Federal Foreign Office guidance for proof of financing for study.

records.claim: The German Opportunity Card can be obtained either by a foreign academic or vocational qualification recognised in Germany or through the points route, which requires a qualifying foreign qualification, language skills and at least six points.
records.sourceAuthority: Make it in Germany / German government
records.methodology: Direct review of current German government information on the Opportunity Card.

records.claim: Opportunity Card applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds for the job-search period; for 2026 this can be shown with a blocked account containing at least €1,091 net per month or through qualifying alternative proof such as a declaration of commitment.
records.sourceAuthority: Make it in Germany / German government
records.methodology: Direct review of current German government Opportunity Card requirements.

records.claim: The France student route is for eligible foreign students admitted to study in France, with the exact visa and supporting-document requirements depending on the applicant's situation and country.
records.methodology: Direct review of current official France-Visas student guidance.

records.claim: For long-stay student visa applications submitted from 1 August 2026, France-Visas states that applicants must provide proof of resources corresponding to at least €877.50 per month.
records.methodology: Direct review of the current official France-Visas student campaign notice.

records.claim: France's Talent Passport routes cover several qualifying talent situations; the highly qualified employee route requires a qualifying higher-education qualification or comparable professional experience and an employment contract meeting the route conditions.
records.methodology: Direct review of current official France-Visas international talent guidance.

records.claim: France-Visas sets salary or subsistence thresholds for specific Talent Passport categories; the highly qualified employee / EU Blue Card route currently requires salary of at least 1.5 times the annual reference salary of €59,373, while other Talent Passport categories have category-specific thresholds.
records.methodology: Direct review of current official France-Visas international talent guidance.

records.claim: Spain's higher-education study stay route requires admission to a recognised higher-education institution for a full-time programme leading to a recognised higher-education qualification, together with the applicable immigration conditions.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration
records.methodology: Direct review of current Spanish government study-stay requirements.

records.claim: Spain requires study-stay applicants to demonstrate sufficient funds; the maintenance threshold is 100% of IPREM per month for the applicant, with separate family thresholds, unless qualifying accommodation has already been paid.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration
records.methodology: Direct review of current Spanish government study-stay requirements.

records.claim: Spain's international teleworker route is a residence/visa route under the international entrepreneur framework for qualifying remote work arrangements, subject to the applicable statutory and documentary conditions.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration
records.methodology: Direct review of the current Spanish government UGE authorisations and requirements page and official international teleworker guidance.

records.claim: Spain's international teleworker applicants must demonstrate sufficient work-derived economic resources; the principal applicant threshold is 200% of the Spanish minimum wage, with additional family thresholds of 75% for the first accompanying family member and 25% for each additional member under the applicable guidance.
records.sourceAuthority: Spanish Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration
records.methodology: Direct review of current Spanish government interpretive guidance for international teleworker economic resources.
